newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens to boost gas output, attract investments.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens to boost gas output, attract investments.

text.p: Turkmenistan aims to nearly double its natural gas output in the long term with the help of foreign investment, Oil & Gas Industry & Mineral Resources Minister Gochmurad Nazdzhanov said on Tuesday.
"In the future, we aim to produce around 85 billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas (annually)," he told journalists at the opening of the Turkmenistan International Oil and Gas 1997 Projects Exhibition.
Gas output is officially targeted at 44 bcm in 1997, after output fell to 35 bcm in 1996. Exports this year are expected to reach 40 bcm from 24 bcm in 1996.
Nazdzhanov said the government had taken concrete steps to attract investment in the oil and gas sector.
"Already we have a law in place where every point is set out in concrete terms," he said. "Foreign investors used not to know exactly what the terms (of deals in Turkmenistan) were."
The former Soviet republic sits on vast reserves of oil and gas, which Nazdzhanov estimated at 6.5 billion tonnes and 21 trillion cubic metres respectively.
But export routes are limited, keeping a cap on output.
Nazdzhanov said the key to the success was getting oil and gas to world markets.
"Producing oil and gas is one problem, but the main problem is getting earnings for that oil and gas," he said.
The former Soviet republic relies on Russia's pipeline system for its gas exports, which typically account for around 60 percent of Turkmenistan's total export earnings.

Of total planned gas exports in 1997, 20 bcm will go to Western European consumers and 20 bcm to members of the former Soviet Union, in line with a deal struck last year between Turkmenistan and Russian gas monopoly Gazprom.
Nazdzhanov said construction on a pipeline supplying Turkmen gas to power plants in Iran was on schedule, and that first deliveries would take place in September or October.
The 200-km (130-mile) Korpedzhe-Kurt-Kuyi pipeline is expected to supply Iran with two bcm of Turkmen gas in its first year, rising to eight bcm a year in 10 years.
Nazdzhanov said other gas pipeline routes, including one across Afghanistan to Pakistan and India, were under discussion.

Unocal Corp of the United States has teamed up with Delta Oil Co of Saudi Arabia for a proposed trans-Afghan gas route, but construction of the pipeline still hinges on international recognition of the Afghan government.
The pipeline, which is initially targeted for Pakistan but may extend to India, could carry up to 20 bcm annually.
Nazdzhanov said Turkmenistan had yet to settle a row with Azerbaijan over disputed sovereignty of some Caspian oil reserves already under development by an $8 billion international consortium.
"This is still an open question," he said. "We are working on this problem with Azerbaijan."

Turkmenistan's oil refining industry had succeeded in attracting major foreign investment, Nazdzhanov said, adding that upgrading plants would help bring the quality of Turkmen oil products up to international standards.
--Mike Collett-White, Ashgabat Newsroom, via +7095 941 8520
